Subject: Quick: network path options for on-prem LLM inference

Karthik —

Thanks for taking this. We’re evaluating Redwood Private for an on-prem deployment that will keep PHI inside our network. High-level constraints:
- Expected steady-state: ~600 qps of short requests (avg 32 tokens) during business hours; burst to ~2k qps.
- Latency target: 50-80ms p99 for token serving (customer-facing).
- Must avoid routing PHI over public endpoints if we can help it.

Can you sketch tradeoffs between: VPC peering, PrivateLink (interface endpoints), and S2S VPN for a setup where Redwood is in our cloud account but we want strong isolation? Specifically: security posture, failure modes, operational complexity, and any pricing surprises.

Also include any docs or attachments you think help.

Appreciate it — happy to jump on a 30m sync after your note.

Alex
NetOps, StratagemHealth

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Quick: network path options for on-prem LLM inference

Alex —

Thanks, good constraints. Attached a short sketch (connectivity-options-v1.pdf) and a latency/SLA worksheet (latency-sla-matrix.xlsx). High-level bullets below; happy to elaborate on a call.

Summary tradeoffs (short):
- VPC Peering:
  - Pros: Lowest operational latency (L3 route), straightforward routing, no endpoint objects to manage. Good for high-throughput, low-latency; costs are mainly cross-AZ/data-transfer.
  - Cons: Cross-account peering scales poorly across many customer VPCs (route table management), no private endpoint abstraction (all routes are open unless careful ACLs). Harder to do multi-region fallbacks.

- PrivateLink (Interface Endpoints):
  - Pros: Strong isolation (endpoint per service), fine-grained security (SGs), easier to audit and restrict; no VPC routing table changes across accounts. Stable DNS and works well with strict security teams.
  - Cons: Per-endpoint ENIs and throughput/connection limits; potential for slightly higher latency than peering due to extra hop. Pricing is per ENI/hour + data processing in some clouds. Better when number of connections is moderate and security trumps raw latency.

- Site-to-Site VPN (IPsec):
  - Pros: Works for customers who won’t permit cross-account networking. Easier to stand up quickly without provider console changes; supports encrypted tunnel over public internet.
  - Cons: Higher and variable latency; less predictable for p99 token SLOs. Throughput limited per tunnel, need multiple tunnels and pathing for high qps. Operational burden: rotation of pre-shared keys, monitoring tunnel flaps.

Risk notes:
- If PHI cannot leave your VPC even transiently, PrivateLink + strict SGs or Dedicated (single-tenant GPU) with peering inside your account is safest.
- For p99 <= 80ms we typically recommend peering inside the same region where possible; PrivateLink can meet targets but requires sizing and testing (ENI throttles can surface under sudden burst).

Recommended approach for StratagemHealth (proposal):
1) Pilot: start with PrivateLink to validate security posture and routing simplicity for NetOps. Use an autoscaled endpoint pool and instrument ENI metrics.
2) Performance pilot: run a subset of production traffic over a peered VPC inside your account (or a dedicated peering arrangement) to measure true p99 under load.
3) Final: choose PrivateLink for regulated workloads + peering for bulk low-latency internal services; fallback S2S VPN only for DR where inter-region peering isn't available.

Action items:
- Alex / NetOps: share expected subnets and any IP allowlists.
- We: send a one-page runbook for failover and ENI sizing by EOD.

I'm copying Kimberly and Marissa to flag operational and pricing implications.

-karthik
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Looping in pricing and onboarding notes. Quick clarifications:
- PrivateLink has provider-side ENI limits: in our managed PrivateLink offering we recommend at least 3 endpoint instances per AZ for burst isolation. That's an operational cost and a per-hour charge; include this in the estimate.
- For peering inside a customer account (we offer a BYO-network model), data egress stays within the cloud fabric and is cheaper than cross-region S2S egress; we should capture typical monthly transfer costs for 600 qps -> 2k qps.

Also, add a note about observability: peering requires VPC flow logs + our tracing; PrivateLink gives us clearer per-endpoint metrics which is handy for capacity planning.

Kimberly
